Academic Affairs Leadership Updates

By Shewanee Howard-Baptiste, Provost

Provost Howard-Baptiste

I am delighted to share two important leadership updates that take effect in August 2026.

Please join me in congratulating Dr. Sarah Adams, who will serve as Interim Dean of Curriculum in addition to her role as Executive Director of General Education. This appointment builds naturally on Sarah's outstanding leadership of our general education program and her collaborative work with the Committee on General Education and the Academic Program Council. Her experience, insight, and commitment to academic excellence will be invaluable as we continue to advance our curricular initiatives.

I am also pleased to celebrate Dr. Mary Robert Garrett, whose transition to Associate Provost and Dean of Faculty is now officially in effect.

“Their leadership will help shape the future of Academic Affairs while ensuring that faculty success and student learning remain at the center of our work.”

Provost Shewanee Howard-Baptiste

In this expanded role, Mary Robert will continue her exceptional work supporting faculty development while partnering more closely with Academic Affairs leadership on faculty support, academic policy, and initiatives that strengthen the faculty experience and advance the College's mission.

Both Sarah and Mary Robert bring extraordinary talent, dedication, and vision to these roles. Their leadership will help shape the future of Academic Affairs while ensuring that faculty success and student learning remain at the center of our work.

Please join me in congratulating Mary Robert and Sarah in wishing them success in these important leadership roles.

Dr. Adams
Dr. Garrett

Provost Advisory Council

By Shewanee Howard-Baptiste, Provost

Academic Affairs is pleased to launch the Provost Advisory Council, a confidential group of faculty and staff who will serve as trusted advisors to the Provost and represent perspectives from across the campus community. Members will offer thoughtful feedback, strategic insight, and forward-looking recommendations that foster innovation, collaboration, and academic excellence across the institution.

Know someone whose perspective would strengthen this work? Nominate yourself or a colleague by sending names to Shewanee. Please include PAC as the subject line and share names by Friday, September 4th: howardbaptistes@berea.edu.

Announcement

Berea Faculty and Staff Participating in AAC&U's Institute on AI, Pedagogy, and the Curriculum

By Shewanee Howard-Baptiste, Provost

Beginning this fall, Drs. Sarah Adams and Rob Smith are co-leading Berea's institutional team in the year-long AAC&U Institute on AI, Pedagogy, and the Curriculum. The team, comprised of Abby Houston, Dr. Tréon McClendon, Joe Murphy, and Dr. Carlos Poggio, will develop a campus AI action plan exploring opportunities and avenues for integrating AI across pedagogy, curriculum, and institutional operations.

As this work progresses, initial plans and recommendations will be shared with the Berea community, with opportunities for broad-based discussion and participation. We look forward to future updates from this team!

Announcement

Berea Joins AI Ready Network: September Webinar Series on AI in the Flow of Work Begins Sept. 10!

Berea College is beginning its participation in AI Ready, a national initiative of the Council of Independent Colleges that offers free monthly webinars for faculty, staff, and administrators building a working understanding of generative AI. The emphasis is on application rather than speculation: practical strategies you can use now.

September's three-part series, AI in the Flow of Work, explores everyday uses such as drafting and refining communications, preparing for meetings, synthesizing research, and cleaning data, along with the practices that keep that use responsible, including human review, data privacy, and accessibility. Sessions run Thursdays, Sept. 10, 17, and 24, from 2:00 to 3:00 PM Eastern. There is no cost to attend, and one registration covers the series: Register here.

For those who would like to watch together as a community, a space will be reserved from 2:00 to 4:00 PM for group viewing, with the hour after each webinar given over to lively discussion and sharing ideas about AI and its appropriate role in our teaching and our everyday work. The exact location is still being determined and will be announced in a follow-up email and in the next issue of this newsletter.

Questions? Contact Rob Smith (smithro@berea.edu), Berea's AI Ready contact.

Insights on the A-word

Mapping the Path Toward Student Success

By Rob Smith

Welcome back to a new academic year! I hope your summer was a restful one and your courses and programs are all getting off to strong starts. I also want to extend a warm welcome to both our returning and new faculty and staff joining our campus community this term.

The start of the year is a natural time to think about our programs, making it a great opportunity to engage in curriculum mapping. If you haven't used it before, curriculum mapping is a collaborative process that simply helps you see "where we teach what" in our programs. Programmatically, it helps us check vertical coherence (i.e., how skills and knowledge are progressively introduced, reinforced, and mastered) as well as horizontal coherence that ensures key concepts are integrated across courses & programming instead of being left in isolated pockets of the curriculum. The collaborative process of building these maps lets us more easily spot gaps, reduce unnecessary overlap, and align our class and programmatic activities with broader program goals.

For our students, seeing a clear map of the curriculum they're asked to navigate can be incredibly helpful. The map acts as an "advance organizer," visually charting their academic journey to reduce cognitive load and clarify the relevance of individual courses and/or programs. By showing how courses or programming build upon one another, it empowers students to make much more informed, intentional decisions about their courses and the activities in which they participate.

To support you in this, you will soon receive a new, user-friendly curriculum mapping tool. This digital template is designed to let your department or program quickly develop, visualize, and maintain your own maps without any administrative hassle. It's a single HTML file that will open in any browser window and comes pre-populated with all of your SLOs/PLOs and courses from the most current Catalog.

I encourage you to explore the tool once it arrives and give mapping a try this term. Please feel free to reach out to me directly with any questions or if you want to talk about mapping strategies. I hope you'll find this a useful and insightful part of your regular assessment process.

Spotlight

Building Community, Developing Leaders: Erica Woods Steps into New Role

By Travis J. Albritton (TJ)

One of the highlights of this summer was working alongside Erica Woods to facilitate a series of conversations with our newest Berea Corps staff. Using We Can't Talk About That at Work as our guide, we created space to explore what it means to engage difficult conversations with greater confidence, curiosity, and care. Throughout the series, Erica brought a thoughtful and practical approach, helping participants develop language and tools they can carry into their work across campus.

I'm delighted to share that Erica is now fully in her role as our new Associate Director of Community Engagement and Leadership Development. Her coaching background, commitment to community, and gift for helping people grow make her an incredible asset to our students and staff. I could not be more excited about the work ahead and the ways Erica will help shape and strengthen community engagement and leadership development across our campus.

Feature

Syllabus Guidelines

By Sarah Adams, Executive Director of General Education and Interim Dean of Curriculum

Per the Faculty Manual:

"Each instructor is expected to prepare and distribute to students at the beginning of each term a syllabus for the course in which they are enrolled. The syllabus is to contain the following information:

  • Course goals
  • Course requirements
  • Nature of course content
  • Methods of evaluation, including the approved description of the College's grading system, and how the instructor will determine a student's grade
  • Course attendance policy
  • Office hours
  • Disability statement

Course goals are expected to center on desired student outcomes. Requirements should be clearly expressed. Material to be covered during the term should be summarized, though a class period-by-period outline need not be provided. The syllabus should make clear the instructor's expectations regarding class attendance, describe any consequences for excessive absences, and specify any instances in which absences may be excused."

Announcement

Give Your Course a GIFT!

Would you like to get midsemester feedback from your students? Joe Murphy, Director of Educational Development, can come to your course and facilitate the Group Instructional Feedback Technique (GIFT). In this ~30-minute session, students will reflect on what is supporting their learning well, and how they think things might improve. They'll discuss as a group, so they can consider their own experiences and others'. Joe will give you an anonymized summary of the class's opinions and meet with you to discuss, and you'll debrief with the students to keep the conversation going.

A GIFT session is a great way to check your impressions of how a class is going, have transparent conversations about the choices you make as a professor, and build a constructive class environment.

To sign up, fill out the form and Joe will be in touch!

Snacks & Strategizing: Mid-Career Mentoring Program for 2026-2027

By Mary Robert Garrett, Associate Provost and Dean of Faculty

I'm delighted to invite you to Snacks & Strategizing: Mid-Career Mentoring, a new series launching this academic year to support one of the most important and most overlooked stages of a faculty career: the years between tenure and full professor.

We'll gather in Draper 307 over coffee, tea, and snacks for focused, low-pressure conversations on the topics that matter most right now. Each session stands on its own, so please join whichever topics speak to you; you don't need to attend every one to belong at any one.

Updates & Announcements

Attendance Tracking

Please use the Attendance Tracker to take attendance in your course. By entering your attendance into the Attendance Tracker, Academic Affairs can easily access the information we need for enrollment and financial aid records as well as for supporting the student support efforts of the NEST.

Non-Attendance on First Day of Class

Instructors may drop any student who doesn't attend the first day of class and doesn't provide advance notice of their absence. If you would like to drop a student who does not attend the first day of your course, please email the Office of the Registrar and provide the student's name and B#.

Future Hire in Academic Affairs

Academic Affairs will post a Dean-level position in fall 2026 to support the division and advance key academic priorities. This re-envisioned role will carry forward many of the responsibilities previously held by the Dean of Curriculum.

I also want to thank Dr. Scott Steele for his leadership and partnership, particularly during my first year as Provost. We are grateful for his many contributions and wish him a rewarding sabbatical.

Upload Syllabuses to the Syllabus Repository

Please follow that link to upload the syllabus for each of your courses by Aug. 22. If you encounter technical problems, please reach out to Scott Heggen; if you do not see your course listed, please email Anna Stamper.
